_note: Ground truth was written from the fixture source, not from any model answer. Facts are atomic; the judge marks each present or absent.

read.prompt: How many times does the service try to send a reminder before giving up, and where is that set?
mustHave: The number is 5 attempts (attempts: 5)
It is set in src/scheduler.js, in tick(), on the withRetry call
src/retry.js has its own default of 3 attempts, which the scheduler overrides

read.prompt: Walk me through what happens from the moment a user creates a reminder until it is delivered.
mustHave: api.js converts the user's local time to a UTC timestamp (toUtcMs) on create and stores the row through db.js
scheduler.js tick() runs on a timer (every 30 seconds) and picks the unsent reminders that are due
Delivery goes through withRetry (retry.js) and notify.js, which loads the formatter named in config.json
A reminder is marked sent only after a successful send; if all retries fail it stays unsent and is tried again on the next tick

read.prompt: Users in India (UTC+5:30) say their reminders arrive about 5 hours before the time they set. UTC users are fine. What is causing it?
mustHave: The offset is applied twice: api.js toUtcMs already converts to UTC, and scheduler.js dueReminders subtracts tz_offset_min again
The faulty line is in dueReminders in src/scheduler.js
East-of-UTC users get reminders early by their offset (5h30m for IST), and west-of-UTC users get them late
The existing tests miss it because the scheduler tests only use a UTC offset of 0

read.prompt: Reminders are lost when the process restarts. Compare realistic ways to make storage persistent and recommend one.
mustHave: Recommends an embedded single-file database such as SQLite (not a database server like Postgres, and not Redis)
Justifies the pick with the deployment: one process on one VM and under about 5,000 reminders
Notes that db.js already exposes a SQL-style query() interface, so swapping in a SQL store needs small changes to callers

read.prompt: Review src/api.js. What are the real problems?
mustHave: SQL injection in searchReminders: userId and q are concatenated into the SQL string instead of passed as parameters
No validation of `at` or tzOffsetMin: a malformed date gives a NaN due_ms, so the reminder never fires
No authentication or ownership check: userId comes from the caller, so anyone can list or search any user's reminders and delete any reminder by id

read.prompt: We want per-user quiet hours, for example 22:00 to 07:00 local time, when reminders are held and sent after the window ends. Plan the change. Don't write any code.
mustHave: There is no per-user settings storage today (only user_id on reminders), so it needs a new table or store and an API endpoint to set quiet hours (db.js, api.js)
Enforcement belongs in the scheduler (dueReminders or tick), using the user's tz_offset_min to get their local time
The window crosses midnight (22:00 to 07:00), so the check must handle wrap-around
The scheduler's double timezone offset bug should be fixed first, or the local-time math will be wrong

read.prompt: Is it safe to delete src/legacy.js?
mustHave: No. notify.js loads formatters dynamically with import(`./${name}.js`), so a search for static imports does not find legacy.js
config.json sets the formatter to "legacy" (and notify.js defaults to 'legacy'), so deleting it breaks every notification at runtime
The tests would not catch it: notify.test.js only uses the 'format' formatter

read.prompt: Why does retry.js add jitter, and is its implementation right?
mustHave: Jitter spreads retries out so many failing sends do not all retry at the same instant (thundering herd)
Bug: jitter is added after the cap, so the delay can exceed maxDelayMs (by up to 500 ms)
Bug: the fixed +/-500 ms jitter is larger than the early backoff (200 ms at attempt 0), so the delay can go negative
Fix: scale the jitter to the delay and/or clamp the result between 0 and maxDelayMs

read.prompt: Give me an overview of this codebase for a new engineer.
mustHave: A small Node 20 ES-module service with no dependencies, tested with node:test
api.js handles create, list, search and delete, and stores reminders through db.js, an in-memory stand-in for a SQL database
A scheduler timer (scheduler.js) finds due reminders and delivers them through notify.js with retry.js backoff; the formatter is chosen in config.json
All data is held in memory and is lost on restart

read.prompt: Where are the test coverage gaps? Which ones matter most?
mustHave: scheduler tick() (the send, mark-sent and failure path) has no tests; only dueReminders is tested
The scheduler tests only use a UTC offset of 0, so timezone handling is not tested
The search endpoint in api.js (the one that concatenates SQL) has no test
retry.js delay bounds and jitter are not tested (the tests stub randomness so there is no jitter)

fix.prompt: Users east of UTC (for example India, UTC+5:30) report that reminders fire hours early. Find the cause and fix it. Add a regression test, and run `node --test test/` to confirm everything passes.
The search endpoint in src/api.js builds its SQL by string concatenation. Fix it. Add a test, and run `node --test test/` to confirm everything passes.
In src/retry.js the jitter can push the delay below 0 or above maxDelayMs. Fix it. Add a test, and run `node --test test/` to confirm everything passes.
